hints: Focus on the two groups attached to each carbon of the C=C double bond, restricted rotation means their positions are fixed.
Check compound 1 first: the left C has CH3 and H, while the right C has CH3 and C2H5, so both ends have two different groups.
Now apply the same two-different-groups test to compounds 2 and 3 to see if all three can exist as cis and trans forms.
walkthrough:
**Recall the condition for cis-trans isomerism**

Think of the C=C bond as locked in place with no rotation. For isomerism, each C of the double bond must have two different groups attached.

Rule: $\text{each C of C=C must have two different substituents}$

**Test compound 1**

Look at $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$. Left C has $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{H}$, which are different. Right C has $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$, which are different.

So compound 1 shows geometrical isomerism.

**Test compound 2**

Look at $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Left C has $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{H}$, which are different. Right C has $\text{H}$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which are different.

So compound 2 shows geometrical isomerism.

**Test compound 3 and conclude**

Look at $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH}=\text{CHC}_2\text{H}_5$. Left C has $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ and $\text{H}$, right C has $\text{H}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$. Both ends have two different groups.

So compound 3 also shows geometrical isomerism. Therefore 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct, because all three alkenes meet the condition. Each C=C carbon carries two different groups, so cis and trans arrangements are possible in every case.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination leaves out compound 3. Students sometimes think a symmetrical alkene like hex-3-ene cannot show isomerism, but the two ethyl groups can still be on the same side (cis) or opposite sides (trans).
options.C: Incorrect. This combination leaves out compound 1. The trap is thinking the two CH3 groups mean one carbon has identical groups, but they are on different carbons. The right-hand carbon has CH3 versus C2H5, which are different.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests only compound 1 works. It misses that compounds 2 and 3 are classic disubstituted alkenes with H versus an alkyl group on each carbon, which clearly allow cis-trans isomerism.
